CAF FORCE

Canadian Armed Forces FORCE Evaluation

FITNESS TEST

At a glance

FORCE is the Canadian service fitness standard, distinct from specialist selection and FORCE Combat.

FEATURED ACTIVITY20 m rushes80 m total in ≤51 s

What the test includes

  • 20 m rushes — ≤51 s
  • Sandbag lift — 30 × 20 kg in ≤3:30
  • Intermittent loaded shuttles — 400 m in ≤5:21
  • Sandbag drag — 20 m without stopping

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

FORCE is the Canadian service fitness standard, distinct from specialist selection and FORCE Combat.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

ActivityPublished requirementHow it works
20 m rushes≤51 sTwo 40 m return shuttles, lowering to prone at 10 m intervals.
Sandbag lift30 × 20 kg in ≤3:30Lift alternating bags above 1 m; the two bags are spaced 1.25 m apart.
Intermittent loaded shuttles400 m in ≤5:21Ten 40 m return shuttles, alternating with and without a 20 kg sandbag.
Sandbag drag20 m without stoppingCarry a 20 kg bag and drag at least four bags; exact drag load depends on surface friction.

Scoring and scope

Every component must meet its minimum. A drag performed with different friction cannot establish an equivalent score.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Practise controlled floor transitions and unloaded shuttles first.
  • Use lighter bags for lifting and carries while learning stable technique.
  • Arrange suitable drag equipment and supervision before attempting the prescribed load.

Putting it into a training week

Choose two or three repeatable sessions addressing the listed movements and aerobic demand. Leave recovery between harder efforts; record comparable results rather than testing maximally every week.

Common mistakes

  • Measuring only a single 20 m leg instead of the complete shuttles.
  • Comparing drag results on different surfaces or ignoring the floor transitions.

What to log

Record all four results, bag masses, floor surface and test variant.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.

Visit Canadian Forces Morale and Welfare Services
REFERENCE

Canadian Forces Morale and Welfare Services. (n.d.). Canadian Armed Forces FORCE Evaluation. https://cfmws.ca/sport-fitness-rec/fitness-testing/cmtfe-force-evaluation/force-evaluation/force-evaluation-faqs

Worth knowing

  • Every component must meet its minimum. A drag performed with different friction cannot establish an equivalent score.
  • Independent practice is not an official assessment.
